$comment: Rule catalog — abstention. Standard 17. Carries the first prohibition in the source list: manufacturing a prediction when evidence is insufficient. Abstention is a valid output here, not a failure state — a well-formed abstention record reaches a supported verdict, and these rules exist to keep that door open rather than to police its use.

rules.title: Abstention is available as a valid output
rules.description: The record schema admits an abstention as a first-class output variant, on equal footing with a prediction.
rules.rationale: A system whose output format has no way to say 'no prediction' forces a number in every case, and the numbers it forces are exactly the ones least supported by evidence. Making abstention representable is the precondition for preferring it.
rules.remediation: Restore the abstention variant to schemas/prediction-record.schema.json.

rules.title: An abstention states the standard wording and its reasons
rules.description: An abstention carries the fixed statement, at least one coded reason with detail, and no probability, edge, or expected value.
rules.rationale: Fixed wording makes abstention recognisable mechanically and stops it being softened into something that reads like a weak prediction. The reasons are what make it actionable: an abstention citing a missing data source is a work item, while an unexplained one is a shrug.
rules.remediation: Use the exact statement, give at least one reason with detail, and remove any prediction-only fields.

rules.title: A prediction is never manufactured when the evidence is insufficient
rules.description: A prediction is not issued while the record's own declarations show the evidence is insufficient: critical information missing without justification, data past its freshness window without accounting, a sample below the minimum without justification, or ensemble disagreement above the threshold left undeclared.
rules.rationale: This is the rule the others exist to serve. Each of those conditions is the record admitting a specific inadequacy; predicting anyway converts an honest gap into a confident number, and the number is what gets used. Abstention is always available and is a supported outcome, so nothing forces the manufacture.
rules.remediation: Address the specific insufficiency the evaluator names, or replace the prediction with an abstention citing it.
rules.$assuranceNote: This aggregates conditions the record DECLARES about itself. A record that understates its own gaps — calling decisive information an immaterial gap, or setting a generous freshness window — passes this rule while violating what it stands for. It catches the honest failure, not the motivated one.
